The '''Simons Center for Geometry and Physics''' is a center for theoretical physics and mathematics at [[Stony Brook University]] in  New York. The focus of the center is [[mathematical physics]] and the interface of geometry and physics. It was founded in 2007 by a gift from the [[Simons Foundation|James and Marilyn Simons Foundation]]. The center's current director is physicist [[Luis Álvarez-Gaumé]].

==History==
===Background===
[[James Harris Simons|James H. Simons]] was the chair of the mathematics department at Stony Brook from 1968 to 1976. After deciding to leave academia, he then went on to make billions with his investment firm [[Renaissance Technologies]]. On February 27, 2008 he announced a donation totaling $60 million (including a $25 million gift two years prior) to the mathematics and physics departments. This was the largest single gift ever given to any of the [[State University of New York|SUNY]] schools.<ref name="newyorktimes">{{cite news|last=Arneson|first=Karen W.|title=$60 Million Gift Is a Record, for Stony Brook |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/28/nyregion/28prof.html?_r=1|accessdate=6 September 2010|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=28 February 2008}}</ref> The gift came during Stony Brook's 50th anniversary and shortly after [[Eliot Spitzer|Gov. Spitzer]] announced his commitment to make Stony Brook a “flagship” of the SUNY system that would rival the nation’s most prestigious state research universities.<ref name="pressrelease">{{cite news|title=Stony Brook University Announces $60 Million Gift From Renowned Financier And Former Math Chair James Simons And Wife Marilyn, A Ph.D. Alumna|url=http://commcgi.cc.stonybrook.edu/am2/publish/General_University_News_2/Stony_Brook_University_Announces_60_Million_Gift_From_Renowned_Financier_And_Former_Math_Chair_James_Simons_And_Wife_Marilyn_A_Ph_D_Alumna.shtml|accessdate=6 September 2010|newspaper=Stony Brook Press Release|date=28 February 2008|archive-date=15 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101015033209/http://commcgi.cc.stonybrook.edu/am2/publish/General_University_News_2/Stony_Brook_University_Announces_60_Million_Gift_From_Renowned_Financier_And_Former_Math_Chair_James_Simons_And_Wife_Marilyn_A_Ph_D_Alumna.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> During his announcement speech, Jim Simons said, "From [[Archimedes]] to [[Isaac Newton|Newton]] to [[Einstein]], much of the most profound work in physics has been deeply intertwined with the geometric side of mathematics. Since then, in particular with the advent of such areas as [[quantum field theory]] and [[string theory]], developments in geometry and physics have become if anything more interrelated. The new Center will give many of the world's best mathematicians and physicists the opportunity to work and interact in an environment and an architecture carefully designed to enhance progress. We believe there is a chance that work accomplished at the Center will significantly change and deepen our understanding of the physical universe and of its basic mathematical structure."<ref name=pressrelease /> The Center results from extensive thought and planning between faculty, department chairs, and others, including [[Cumrun Vafa]] of Harvard, who directs the Simons Foundation-supported summer institutes on string theory at Stony Brook, and [[Isadore Singer]] of MIT.<ref name=pressrelease />

===Establishment===
[[John Morgan (mathematician)|John Morgan]] served as the founding director from 2009 to 2016.<ref name="scgp-founding">{{cite web |url=http://scgp.stonybrook.edu/about/a-word-from-the-director/about-the-director-2/the-founding-director |title=The Founding Director |website=Simons Center for Geometry and Physics at [[Stony Brook University]] |accessdate=January 27, 2021}}</ref><ref name="scgp-morgan">{{cite web |url=http://scgp.stonybrook.edu/people/faculty/bios/john-morgan |title=John Morgan |website=Simons Center for Geometry and Physics at [[Stony Brook University]] |accessdate=January 27, 2021}}</ref> [[Luis Álvarez-Gaumé]] has been the director since 2016.<ref name="scgp-alvarez-gaume">{{cite web |url=http://scgp.stonybrook.edu/about/a-word-from-the-director/about-the-director-2 |title=About the Director |website=Simons Center for Geometry and Physics at [[Stony Brook University]] |accessdate=January 27, 2021}}</ref>

==Building==
The Simons Center's building was completed in September 2010. The building is adjacent to the physics and mathematics departments to allow for close collaboration with the mathematics department and the [[C. N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics]]. The  building offers {{convert|40000|sqft|m2}} of floor space, spread over six stories, and includes a 236-seat auditorium, a 90-seat lecture hall, offices,  seminar rooms, and a cafe.<ref name="newsletter">{{cite web|url=http://www.stonybrook.edu/facilities/data/facilities-newsletter-2010-09-30.pdf|title=Stony Brook Facilities & Services newsletter|accessdate=4 October 2010|archive-date=2011-01-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110106171647/http://www.stonybrook.edu/facilities/data/facilities-newsletter-2010-09-30.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> The building is [[Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design|LEED]] Gold certified<ref>{{cite web|title=Simons Center for Geometry and Physics - U.S. Green Building Council|url=http://www.usgbc.org/projects/simons-center-geometry-and-physics|accessdate=19 May 2015}}</ref> and is connected to the Math Tower via an elevated walkway.

==Faculty==
The Center's permanent faculty currently consists of mathematicians [[Simon Donaldson]], [[Kenji Fukaya]], and [[John Pardon]], and physicists [[Nikita Nekrasov]] and [[Zohar Komargodski]]. The Center's academic staff also includes roughly 10 research assistant professors and 20 visiting researchers at any given time.<ref>{{cite web|title=People at the SCGP - Spring 2011|url=http://www.scgp.stonybrook.edu/?q=node/8|accessdate=27 March 2011}}</ref> Other former faculty members include physicists [[Michael R. Douglas]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael R. Douglas – SCGP |url=https://scgp.stonybrook.edu/people/faculty/bios/michael-r-douglas |access-date=2023-09-12 |website=scgp.stonybrook.edu}}</ref> and [[Anton Kapustin]].{{citation needed|date=January 2021}}
